chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Hannan ibn Sadeer, from his father, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: 'The two edges of the Bridge (as-Sirat) on the Day of Resurrection are Kinship (Ar-Rahim) and Trust/Entrustment (Al-Amanah). So when the one who maintains kinship and fulfills the trust passes by, he will pass through to Paradise. And when the betrayer of the trust and the cutter of kinship passes by, no deed will benefit him alongside these two, and the Bridge will fling him into the Fire.'

key_terms.الصِّرَاط: The Bridge over Hellfire on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What are the two edges of the Sirat bridge on the Day of Judgment according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (AS) from the companion Abu Dharr, highlights the dual pillars of social and spiritual integrity: maintaining kinship (Silat al-Rahim) and fulfilling trusts (Al-Amanah). In Shia scholarship, these are often viewed as the external manifestations of internal faith, where severing ties or betraying trust nullifies the efficacy of other good deeds, causing the believer to tip into Hellfire despite their efforts.
